Everything above the generated section is maintained by hand. tests/test_pipeline.py fails if a Python dependency or a script loaded by the site is missing from it, or if the generated section is stale.

About presentation

The 30-second presentation at site/about.html reuses the event data and viewer. Its method diagrams are code-drawn schematics, not additional measurements. Full source-photo verification and provenance are in site/about/README.md and photo-source.json.

  • Schoolyard photograph: Akai, Ota, Maruyama, Yoshimi, Azuma, Ninomiya / Geological Survey of Japan, AIST, Emergency field report No. 5, photo 10. Source report; original photograph; GSJ Terms of Use, CC BY 4.0 compatible. The original 1021 × 767 PNG bytes and annotations are unchanged. Presentation crop/reframing and English caption by Dancing With The SARs; no GSJ endorsement is implied. The 94 cm value is the field survey, not NISAR.
  • Additional animated field photographs: GSJ/AIST report No. 5, photo 11: Yatsushiro Junction and photo 12: Yatsushiro Shrine. Same named report authors and GSJ terms as photo 10 above. Original source images are loaded unchanged; CSS reframing, animation and English captions are by Dancing With The SARs, without GSJ endorsement.
  • Sideways-slip prototype: GSJ field offsets and Nevada Geodetic Laboratory daily positions for GSI GEONET stations. The field between observations is modelled, exaggerated and imperfect; vertical movement is omitted. See the model and sources. It is not radar-measured sideways motion.
  • Radar, Sentinel-2 imagery and terrain carry the satellite-data credits and terms above. The twelve-event mosaic renders twelve actual Copernicus DEM meshes with the committed radar and optical layers in one shared three.js context. Terrain relief is exaggerated ×1–5; plinths are illustrative, not geology. Tile scales differ. Radar is colour, never vertical uplift. This is evidence of pipeline reuse, not twelve independent scientific validations. Static radar previews remain only in the final CTA.

AI ("Super Intelligence") disclosure

We used a combination of AI models and coding agents throughout. They did research for candidate events and ground stories, wrote most of the pipeline and site code, and drafted the docs. Every value and source was checked against the original, and a person makes the editorial choices in the editor.

No documentary photograph, satellite image or map data on the site was generated by AI. The About presentation’s code-drawn method schematics were authored with AI assistance and are labelled as schematics, not observations. Any generative-media image added later must carry a visible label on the image itself (e.g. "SI-generated image via <tool>") and be listed here.

The project's own code and text are released under CC0 1.0 (see LICENSE). Third-party data and media keep their own licences, as listed above and per item.
